name: LED Dot-Matrix Ticker
summary: A physical LED sign scrolls your metrics like a stock ticker until one freezes and inverts into a coral alert block.
look: A screwed dark bezel full of round diodes with the unlit dots faintly visible, 5×7 bitmap letters with a soft bloom in amber, teal, white and coral. The anomaly becomes a solid coral block with the number punched out in dark dots.

components.name: Dot grid
components.role: 80 columns at 12 px pitch, unlit diodes at ~8%

components.name: Bitmap font
components.role: 5×7 glyphs scaled 1×/2×/4× by lighting diode blocks

components.name: Ticker line
components.role: clipped marquee of metric tokens along the top row

components.name: Alert block
components.role: coral cluster with inverted, punched-out anomaly text

components.name: Pixel sparkline
components.role: one diode column per sample, last bars coral

components.name: Bezel & hardware
components.role: housing, fine-pitch caption strip and arcade buttons for the human action

motion.name: Marquee
motion.how: whole-dot 12 px steps at constant linear speed, 8 steps per beat at 120 BPM

motion.name: Diagonal reveal
motion.how: dots light along (x + y) index with 8 ms stagger; the front crosses the panel in one bar

motion.name: Alert blink
motion.how: block toggles 3× on/off at 150 ms, then holds on the next downbeat; bloom is a 5 px blur merged over the dots

story: Hook: an amber ticker scrolls while '38 OPEN TABS TODAY' and a coral '3 READ' light up, the lower strip asks 'How many did you check today?'. Reveal: a diagonal scan front lights ACME / PULSE in teal under a backlit mark plate. Proof: the teal ticker freezes on CHECKOUT, the matrix inverts into a coral block with −18% punched out, amber lines add 'since 09:42' and 'deploy #2231', the sparkline drops and a real ROLL BACK button lights for the human press. CTA: YOU SHIP. / PULSE / WATCHES. with a crawling ticker and a START FREE box that traces its border.
adapt: Put your own live counters in the ticker and your single most important alert in the inverted block; keep lines under 13 characters at 1× scale and let hardware buttons carry the user's action.

fit.risk: can read as a retro gadget rather than a serious tool; keep copy terse and palette strict
